result.title: Correcting or Continuing? What On-Policy Distillation Learns from Student Errors
result.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own rollouts under a frozen teacher, mitigating the distribution mismatch of off-policy supervision. While prior work has primarily trained on problems a student can largely solve, we ask whether OPD can improve a student when training is restricted to problems it currently fails. We evaluate five representative OPD mechanisms with Qwen-3 and Phi-4 models under a unified competition-mathematics protocol. We find that OPD does not improve accuracy on this hard subset, with most mechanisms instead degrading performance despite continued decreases in training KL divergence. All eight configurations show a decline, and the two-sided sign test gives p=0.0078. In contrast, the same pipeline improves accuracy by 4.6 percentage points when training is not concentrated on failures, showing that the failure is conditional on the training regime rather than systematic. These findings suggest that OPD is effective when supervision is dominated by correct student prefixes, but can reinforce existing errors when training is concentrated on problems the student currently fails.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在统一数学竞赛协议下评估 Qwen-3 与 Phi-4 上的五种 on-policy distillation 机制，发现当训练只集中在学生当前做不对的难题上时，准确率不升反降（8 组配置全部下降），而训练不集中于失败集时提升约 4.6 个百分点，说明效果取决于监督是否由正确的学生前缀主导。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本训练监督工作，与 LVR 关注的轨迹训练、贡献分配和监督来源有潜在联系：其失败样本主导的 on-policy 监督会强化既有错误这一现象，可供核查 latent 推理轨迹训练中如何筛选正/负样本与分配监督信号。
